# Browser
## Stop: choose the right surface before any browser action
Explicit browser intent wins: if the user names the in-app browser or Chrome, or asks to open, show, or navigate to a page; inspect its visual or interactive state; or interact with its UI, continue with Browser and do not substitute a connector.

Do not initialize Browser for that operation until the query is complete. Use the non-browser tool when available. If it handles the current operation, continue the larger workflow without Browser for that operation. Use Browser when no such tool exists, the tool cannot access the resource or lacks a required capability, or UI work remains; use available browser context before asking the user to repeat it.

Use this skill for browser automation tasks such as inspecting pages, navigating, testing local apps, clicking, typing, taking screenshots, and reading visible page state.

If this plugin is listed as available in the session, treat that as mandatory reading before browser work. Open and follow this skill before saying that Browser is unavailable and before falling back to standalone Playwright or Computer Use.

Do not skip this skill just because Computer Use MCP tool calls are directly visible or appear easier to invoke. The presence of Computer Use tools is not evidence that Computer Use is the preferred browser surface.

Never mention `Node REPL`, `node_repl`, `REPL`, JavaScript sessions, module exports, reading documentation, or loading instructions unless a user is asking for that exact information. IMPORTANT: If this path cannot be found, stop and report that this plugin is missing `scripts/browser-client.mjs`. NEVER use the built in `browser-client` library.

You need the `js` execution tool: `js_reset` only clears state, and `js_add_node_module_dir` only changes package resolution. Do not call either helper while trying to expose `js`. CODE MODE REQUIREMENT: When you call the Node REPL `js` tool from the code-mode `exec` tool, the outer `exec` script containing the initial `documentation()` call MUST begin with `// @exec: {"max_output_tokens": 20000}`. This is a first-line pragma for the outer `exec` call, not an argument to the nested `js` tool. Initialize the runtime once per fresh Node session. If `agent.browsers` already exists, reuse it; do not import or initialize another browser runtime.

if (globalThis.agent?.browsers == null) {
  const { setupBrowserRuntime } = await import("<plugin root>/scripts/browser-client.mjs");

# VFX Reference Dossier — melee_arc

## Candidate 1: Demon Hand Cleave Effect (Path of Exile)
- source_game: Path of Exile
- skill_or_mtx_name: Demon Hand Cleave Effect
- primary_url: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7_uDBjRX45Y
- secondary_urls: https://www.pathofexile.com/shop/item/DemonHandCleave
- media_type: video
- temporal_coverage: windup=Y; active=Y; impact=Y
- why_it_fits: The weapon swing produces a single, broad demonic-claw swipe across the character’s forward melee sector. Its synchronized body motion and sharply bounded arc are an especially direct expression of arc_sweep geometry.
- readability_notes: The oversized claw silhouette remains recognizable at the standard isometric camera. Its ornamental fingers add visual noise, but the outer arc and facing direction stay clear.

## Candidate 2: Grim Scythe (Diablo III)
- source_game: Diablo III
- skill_or_mtx_name: Grim Scythe
- primary_url: https://news.blizzard.com/en-gb/article/20597129/necromancer-update-the-meleemancer
- secondary_urls: https://bnetcmsus-a.akamaihd.net/cms/gallery/7TXLS1RMYJD71489442888934.gif
- media_type: gif
- temporal_coverage: windup=Y; active=Y; impact=Y
- why_it_fits: Blizzard explicitly presents this as a summoned scythe traveling through a wide arc. The animation cleanly couples a lateral melee gesture with a large crescent-shaped effect and visible enemy contact.
- readability_notes: The summoned blade is substantially larger than the character, making the attack sector legible through combat clutter. Its short duration prevents the effect from obscuring subsequent actions.

## Candidate 3: Demonic Reave Effect (Path of Exile)
- source_game: Path of Exile
- skill_or_mtx_name: Demonic Reave Effect
- primary_url: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=L6S8JrJpfhU
- secondary_urls: https://www.pathofexile.com/shop/item/DemonicReave
- media_type: video
- temporal_coverage: windup=Y; active=Y; impact=Y
- why_it_fits: Each melee gesture releases a broad, forward-facing wave of demonic energy whose leading edge retains a strong curved-sweep character. Repeated casts also demonstrate how an arc effect can scale outward without losing its directional origin.
- readability_notes: The high-contrast rim makes the attack boundary readable from the gameplay camera. The expanding energy body can suggest more range than a strictly close-quarters melee arc, so the leading crescent is the most useful binding reference.

## Candidate 4: Celestial Lacerate Effect (Path of Exile)
- source_game: Path of Exile
- skill_or_mtx_name: Celestial Lacerate Effect
- primary_url: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=_odu2eo6jP0
- secondary_urls: https://www.pathofexile.com/shop/item/CelestialLacerateEffect
- media_type: video
- temporal_coverage: windup=Y; active=Y; impact=Y
- why_it_fits: The showcase exposes paired sweeping slashes that originate at the attacker and cross the forward sector. It is useful for studying a melee_arc rendered as layered crescents rather than one opaque blade trail.
- readability_notes: Bright celestial edges remain distinct against subdued terrain and clearly communicate orientation. Because the slashes propagate outward, this is best used for arc construction and timing rather than strict melee-range calibration.

## Search log
- Searched official Path of Exile YouTube and MTX-shop results for Sweep, Cleave, Lacerate, Reave, and Blade Flurry effects.
- Verified official video and shop URLs for Demon Hand Cleave, Demonic Reave, and Celestial Lacerate.
- Checked Diablo III game-guide and Blizzard News results for Crippling Wave and Grim Scythe; retained Grim Scythe because Blizzard supplies an animated gameplay GIF, while the current Crippling Wave guide page exposes no comparable media.
- Searched Grim Dawn Blade Arc references; found the official wiki description and several player build videos, but no equally isolated official effect showcase.
- Searched Last Epoch and Lost Ark official skill-showcase combinations; no stronger, directly indexed melee-arc clip surfaced.
- Blade Flurry showcases were rejected because their channel-and-release structure communicates a different temporal geometry from a discrete arc sweep.
